analysis.answer_text: Okay, let’s go through a quick, steady troubleshooting routine together.First, restart the basics: turn off your computer’s Wi-Fi, then power off your router and modem, wait about 20 seconds, and power them back on.
analysis.reply_text: First, move closer to the router and note if the drops still happen, because distance and walls can make a weak signal worse. Next, restart your router and modem by unplugging them for about 20 seconds, then plugging them back in and waiting for all the lights to stabilize. Then, on your device, turn Wi-Fi off and back on, and if you see multiple networks, pick the correct one and re-enter the password cleanly. After that, check for interference: if the router is near a microwave, cordless phone base, or crowded spot, move it higher and more in the open. Then update firmware and drivers, using your router’s admin page for firmware and your computer or phone updates for Wi-Fi drivers. Finally, if it still drops, try changing the Wi-Fi channel or switching between 2.4 gigahertz and 5 gigahertz, and if that’s too fiddly, reset the router to factory settings and set it up fresh.
